commits.message: fix(update-act): a held group whose process has exited is dropped from the ⚠ before its write is retried (brandon-unfiled-3248.pj1z)

fix(update-act): an overdue act pruned before its end still has its group ended when its leader proves it, and otherwise shown in the ⚠ until it is gone (brandon-unfiled-3248.pj1z)

When a newer claim removes a timed-out act between the look and the end,
the end now proves the group by its leader's fingerprint and signals it
only on that proof. A group nothing proves is written beside the acts, so
every daemon's ⚠ names it with the command that ends it until it is no
longer the job's. The watch's ⚠ messages are now each their own entry.

fix(edit-chrome): a layout edit releases every held value whose admission it changes, so a re-added placement's configure state is closed (brandon-unfiled-3248.t2yz) (#701)

* test(edit-chrome): a placement re-added under a removed one's freed id finds its after-gap library closed (brandon-unfiled-3248.t2yz)

The layout-op verb already releases, in the removal's own click, every
state key the config declared before the edit and no longer declares, so
the removed placement's after-gap library key is cleared and a placement
minted later under the freed id inherits nothing. This pins the ticket's
done-when end to end: open the library, remove, re-add under the bare id,
and the library reads closed. It fails with that release disabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(edit-chrome): a placement's removed library state is released by any edit that begins or ends its key, so a re-added placement inherits nothing (brandon-unfiled-3248.t2yz)

The layout-op verb released only the keys an edit ends, so a placement
removed by a hand edit left its after-gap library key open, and the click
that re-added the same id did not release it (the key was not declared
before that click). The release now covers the symmetric difference: a
key the edit begins holds nothing the current config wrote, so whatever
it holds is left over from an earlier placement. Still one enforcer, and
still nothing released on reload, so session values outlive a transient
hand edit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(edit-chrome): a layout edit releases every held value whose admission it changes, so a re-added placement's configure state is closed (brandon-unfiled-3248.t2yz)

The release compared declarations, and the configure key is declared by
every config, so a configure value naming a placement removed by hand
survived the click that re-added the same id. The layout-op verb now
reads each stored value under the configs before and after the edit, as
the state gate reads it (undeclared, held, or foreign), and releases
every value the two read differently. That one comparison covers keys
the edit ends, keys it begins, and the configure member, so the ended-
placement walk and its configure clause are gone. Drafts are state-gate
keys (every setting control writes its key through a `set` action), so
the walk's drafts part goes too; the two-preset drafts test still pins
the exact released list.

"Undeclared" is its own reading rather than folded into "not admitted",
so a foreign value in a key the edit ends or begins is still released,
as the declaration rule released it before.

Out of scope: other sessions on the same origin keep their values; that
is brandon-unfiled-3248.ce4m.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(diagnostics): a list with nothing wrong in it draws ℹ N in blue, not an amber ⚠ (brandon-unfiled-3248.gm3h)

A third diagnostic level, info, carried in one level table (rank, the
indicator's glyph, the colours). An update offer, a repository question and
the lane handoff line are info. The indicator wears the list's worst level
and the list runs worst first, so its click opens a message of that level.
A failed update act is a plain warning of its own beside the offer, so the
failure still raises an amber ⚠ while the offer keeps its identity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cache): each catch-up turn takes the most recently used due entry as the map stands (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A session drawn during the walk is now re-read on the next turn, not
where its entry stood when the batch began. A turn clears its handle
before it reloads and arms only when none is armed, so a batch started
inside a turn leaves one walker. A throw is logged with its stack.

fix(cache): a catch-up turn is its own error boundary and walks most recently used first (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

A walk turn runs from setImmediate, outside the watcher registry's
try/catch, so a reload that threw there reached uncaughtException and
shut the daemon down. The turn now logs the throw and arms the next.

The walk takes the most recently used entry first, so the bar in front
of the user is re-read on the first turn. The due set is a Set: every
due entry always reloads for the latest batch's cause, which the armed
turn carries.

fix(cache): a catch-up reloads one entry per turn, so requests are answered between entries (candybar-animation-wbxz.v24)

When file events resumed after a stall, or the repo answers moved, the
render cache reloaded every entry in one synchronous turn. A reload that
keeps its state still resolves, validates and keys the whole chain, so
105 entries held the live daemon's loop for 1.7s on a calm machine and
11s on a loaded one, and every client waiting behind it hung up (the
EPIPE bursts in daemon.log).

The walk now takes one due entry per turn of the loop. Any reload clears
its entry's due mark, a drop clears a dropped entry's, a reload that
throws ends only its own turn, and close cancels the armed turn. The
render cache's stats count the entries still due.
